results.title: Competing claims cover the South China Sea islands.
results.description: Competing claims cover the South China Sea islands. China cites centuries of discovery, naming and use, formalized via 20th-century maps and the nine-dash line. The Philippines relies on proximity, mid-20th-century occupation of certain features and UNCLOS EEZ rights. Vietnam asserts earlier administration. The 2016 arbitration backed Philippine maritime arguments but left sovereignty undecided; China rejects the ruling. Multiple nations occupy features today.

results.title: Vietnam is not a China vessel.
results.description:
Vietnam is not a China vessel. It is a sovereign state with its own independent Communist Party, a long history of resisting Chinese control (including the 1979 border war), and ongoing South China Sea disputes. It hedges economically with China while deepening ties with the US, Japan and others for balance.

Vietnam currently leads in operational electronics manufacturing and assembly scale, with mature clusters and major FDI like Samsung’s $1.5B+ chip testing plant (back-end, not wafer fab). India trails in pure export assembly but is investing heavily in higher-value stages, localization, and semiconductor fabs via PLI and ISM schemes, explicitly aiming for greater independence from Chinese supply chains. Both pursue China+1, yet India restricts Chinese investment more tightly while Vietnam still relies heavily on Chinese intermediates.
